solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Parking in spot by church address

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another is held inside it, so the parking letter goes within the word for spot

parts.note: to spot something is to see it
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A driver leaves the car in a space next to the church's address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' looks like a street location for the church; it is a formal talk.
explanation.definitionFit: An address is a formal talk given to an audience, which is what a speech is.

clue.text: Show nurses fine needle

indicators.note: to nurse something is to hold and cradle it, so one word holds the other inside

parts.note: to show something is to prove it
OK means fine, all right

explanation.surface: A medical drama displays a nurse handling a hypodermic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nurses' and 'needle' set up a hospital scene; nurses is the container signal and needle a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to irritate or goad them, a close synonym of provoke.

clue.text: 100% up — time to break out

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading the word from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: something 100% is pure, unadulterated
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Everything is ready, so it is time to escape.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcano or a rash that erupts breaks out suddenly, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: The man deals with Top Gear items?

parts.note: the pronoun for a man is he
to address a problem is to deal with it

explanation.surface: Jeremy Clarkson handles the business on the motoring show Top Gear.
explanation.walkthrough: Top Gear is a BBC motoring programme, but here 'top gear' is read as clothing worn on top, that is on the head; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Headdresses are worn on top of the head, so they are literally gear for the top.

clue.text: Complexity of records given to judge

parts.note: tapes are recordings
to try a case is to judge it; 'given to' just puts it after

explanation.surface: Recordings handed to a judge are complicated evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapestry is figuratively an intricate interwoven whole, as in the rich tapestry of life, so it stands for complexity.

clue.text: Piece of bread in cream tart

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it, so the bread goes within the cream word

parts.note: the cream is the top, the best part, as cream rises to the top of milk
a roll is a single small loaf

explanation.surface: A baker's description of a cake: a bit of bread in a cream tart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' is not the pastry here but the old derogatory word for a promiscuous woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Trollop and tart are both dated, insulting words for a promiscuous woman.

clue.text: Couple ending up with one letter

indicators.note: a couple of endings means the last letter of each of two words is taken

parts.note: the final letters of the two words
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A pair finally get together, with one of them sending a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Phi is the twenty-first letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Dance music, being funky, is cracking hit

indicators.note: funky suggests something jazzed up and rearranged, so the letters are reworked
something cracking another breaks into it, so it sits inside the other word

parts.note: to swat is to hit
the letters of being, rearranged

explanation.surface: A DJ praises a funky dance track as a cracking hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracking hit' reads as praise for a record; in fact the jumbled word breaks into SWAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Swingbeat, also called new jack swing, is a style of dance music blending R&B and hip-hop.

clue.text: Annoyed with joint, in a way

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it, so the joint goes within the abbreviation for a way

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
the ankle is a joint of the leg

explanation.surface: Someone is irritated by a joint, perhaps a painful one, in some way.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rankled caused lasting resentment, so it annoyed, in the past tense like the clue.

clue.text: Consensus of 26?

parts.note: surface reading: the general agreement about a case, the answer at 26; setter's reading: the answer at 26 splits into a word for in fashion and a word for a point of view, so it is a definition-by-example of this phrase

explanation.surface: A query about what everyone thinks of a particular case.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: INSTANCE at 26 is IN (popular) plus STANCE (opinion), so 26 is itself wordplay for POPULAR OPINION.
explanation.definitionFit: Popular opinion is what most people think, which is a consensus.

clue.text: Sausage roll made at random

indicators.note: at random means in no set order, so these letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A deli sandwich: a sausage roll made up on a whim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sausage roll' looks like one thing; 'roll' is in fact part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Mortadella is a large Italian pork sausage from Bologna, served sliced.

clue.text: Kids like to keep hand on nose

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so the outer word holds the rest inside

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of
to dole out is to hand out
to nose is to smell out, to scent

explanation.surface: Children, typically, hold a hand over their noses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' just places the nose word after the hand word; 'hand' and 'nose' are both verbs here, not body parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Adolescents are teenagers, still kids in the informal sense of young people.

clue.text: Swallow, one that stops returning

indicators.note: something returning goes back the way it came, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: a plug is something that stops up a hole

explanation.surface: A swallow is a bird that comes back each year, not leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' and 'returning' suggest the migrating bird; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To gulp is to swallow quickly in large mouthfuls.

clue.text: Iron rod and spade to cut grass

indicators.note: a thing that cuts another goes into it, splitting it, so the letter sits inside

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
S is the abbreviation for spades in card games
a cue is the rod used in snooker

explanation.surface: Gardening kit, an iron rod and a spade, used to cut the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut grass' reads as mowing; the cutting is the spade letter splitting the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Fescue is a genus of grasses, widely used for lawns and pasture.

clue.text: Violent act due to power being seized

definitions.text: Violent act due to power being seized

indicators.note: something seized is held fast, so the power letter is held inside the rearranged letters
a violent act is a disorderly one, so its letters are thrown about

parts.note: the letters of these three words
P is the abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A violent act takes place because power has been seized.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a coup is exactly a violent act in which power is seized.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup d'etat is the sudden, often violent seizure of state power by a small group.

clue.text: Take or takes steps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the takings, money raised by an event
second meaning: goes forward, moves on

explanation.surface: A choice between seizing something or acting on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take' looks like a verb but is the noun, as in the box-office take.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means money earned; as a verb it means advances or acts.

clue.text: Damned useless cue cards

indicators.note: useless suggests broken and out of order, so the letters must be reworked

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A presenter curses prompt cards that are no help.
explanation.definitionFit: Accursed means under a curse, damned, or more loosely hateful.

clue.text: Tank command is initially tough

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of the words before it

parts.note: the first letters of these two words
stern means tough, severe

explanation.surface: An army tank commander is tough from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tank command' suggests the military; the tank holds water.
explanation.definitionFit: A cistern is a tank for storing water, as above a toilet.

clue.text: A remedy for change that's unfortunate

indicators.note: something put up for change is to be altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A cure for change sounds like bad news for someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Deary me is an exclamation of mild dismay, said when something is unfortunate.

clue.text: One car is all you have

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a type of car with a long rear load space
second meaning: a person's total property and assets

explanation.surface: A modest owner whose only possession is a single car.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate car is the British name for what Americans call a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a car with a large rear compartment and, separately, everything a person owns, especially at death.

clue.text: Foot that is trapped under pipes

parts.note: to pipe on an instrument is to toot
i.e. is the abbreviation of Latin id est, that is

explanation.surface: A foot got stuck under some plumbing.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'under' puts IE below TOOTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tootsie is a playful childish word for a foot or toe.

clue.text: Got through American education

parts.note: US is short for American
Ed is the abbreviation for education

explanation.surface: Someone graduated through the American school system.
explanation.definitionFit: Having used something up is having got through it, as with supplies, so the past tenses match.

clue.text: Break away? No

parts.note: surface reading: someone refusing to escape or secede; setter's reading: a break, a holiday, that is not spent away from home

explanation.walkthrough: 'Break away' reads as escaping; split it into a break that is away, then deny the away.
explanation.definitionFit: A staycation is a holiday taken at home or in one's own country rather than travelling abroad.

clue.text: Extremity, but not one on claw

indicators.note: but not one means without the numeral one, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: the tail is an extremity of an animal
the Roman numeral for one, to be removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: An animal's extremity, but not the one with a claw on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A talon is the hooked claw of a bird of prey.

clue.text: Words from mouth?

parts.note: surface reading: anything someone says, speech from a person's mouth; setter's reading: the mouth of a river, specifically the Thames, so speech typical of that region

explanation.walkthrough: The Thames estuary is the river's mouth, east of London; the accent named after it is a mix of Cockney and standard southern English.
explanation.definitionFit: This term names the accent spoken around the Thames estuary in south-east England, words literally from the river mouth.

clue.text: 18's name for bristle

parts.note: the answer at 18 is an exclamation of dismay, and aw is another
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Someone asks what 18 calls a bristle.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is DEARY ME; AW is an equivalent exclamation, followed by N.
explanation.definitionFit: An awn is a bristle-like spike growing from the grain husk of barley and many grasses.

clue.text: Case against ancestor being keeper

indicators.note: a keeper holds something inside, so the words keep the solution within them

parts.note: running across the two words

explanation.surface: A lawsuit brought against a forebear who held some keeping role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' and 'against' suggest a court action; the letters span the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is an example or case, as in 'in this instance'.

clue.text: Bob's secret — a bad one

parts.note: a bob is an old British shilling, abbreviated s
inner means private, secret, as in inner thoughts

explanation.surface: Bob, a man, has a bad secret.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob looks like a man's name; it is slang for a shilling, the pre-1971 British coin, abbreviated s.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinner is a wrongdoer, someone bad in the moral sense.
